title: The Serengeti & Masai Mara: East Africa's great plains
excerpt: The Great Migration, balloon safaris at dawn and the culture of the Maasai — a guide to the plains of Kenya and Tanzania.

body.p: The Serengeti in Tanzania and the Masai Mara in Kenya are two halves of one vast ecosystem. These are the endless plains of the documentaries: flat-topped acacias, big skies, and some of the greatest concentrations of wildlife left on earth.

Each year well over a million wildebeest, joined by zebra and gazelle, follow the rains in a great circle through the Serengeti and into the Mara. Calving takes place on the southern Serengeti plains early in the year, and the dramatic river crossings in the north usually happen between July and October. Wildlife movements vary from year to year, so crossings are never guaranteed — but the plains are full of life in every month.

body.p: The Maasai have lived alongside wildlife on these plains for generations. A respectful visit to a Maasai village — with its beadwork, songs and the famous jumping dance — is often a highlight, and the best visits support the community directly.

The Masai Mara is compact and easy to reach from Nairobi, making it perfect for a shorter first safari. Tanzania's Serengeti is larger and wilder, and combines beautifully with the Ngorongoro Crater and the beaches of Zanzibar. Both pair well with time on the Indian Ocean coast.

Light-aircraft flights between airstrips often have luggage limits, so pack in a soft bag. Both countries have specific health and entry requirements — check visas, vaccinations and malaria advice with a travel doctor before you book.
